additional_primary_sources.section: NOTES / Use cases for PID file descriptors
additional_primary_sources.claim: Current manual distinguishes readable exit notification from hangup after reaping; without PIDFD_THREAD completion waits for the whole thread group.
Pinned proc descriptors do not act on a later process reusing the numeric PID.

source_findings.summary: io is owner-read-only; task_dump_owner chooses root ownership with no mm. exit_mm clears mm before exit_notify assigns EXIT_ZOMBIE. The interval can therefore expose EACCES on io open with a non-Z stat state to an unprivileged reader.

io show has a separate ptrace access check. Its mm dumpability condition is guarded by non-null mm; mm==NULL is not itself the ptrace denial branch. Historical operation was open, so owner/mode denial is a plausible explanation, not a proven stack trace.

v6.8.12 pidfd_poll returns IN|RDNORM on whole-group exit, including when no task remains. It has no HUP branch. Current official manual also defines HUP after reaping. Accepting IN or HUP on an authenticated pidfd is compatible; neither HUP nor both bits is required.

historical_scope.known_operation: open relative io through pinned proc directory

binding_order: read initial stat from pinned directory; compare expected start
poll pidfd with zero timeout and record live binding before details
recommended_contract.binding_invariant: A nonready pidfd after matching pinned stat establishes that the pidfd has not fully terminated before the proc binding. Do not combine a ready old pidfd with a new numeric PID directory. start_ticks is a coarse identity check, not a kernel object reference.
recommended_contract.ready_at_binding: Retain the ordinary pinned same-identity terminal Z/X handling. Do not enable new live-to-exit recovery without completed live binding; record ambiguous binding conservatively.
recommended_contract.deadline_clock: monotonic; fixed deadline, no extension on EINTR
recommended_contract.error_gate: only process io EACCES; no IO reread, no synthesized zero
recommended_contract.immediate_recheck: Retain raw state and errors on every outcome. Same-identity Z/X keeps the existing terminal path. For already-live-bound pidfd, same-identity nonterminal state may await exit proof. A narrowly recorded ENOENT/ESRCH can also use already-bound pidfd proof, but is never proof alone.
recommended_contract.final_recheck: Use only original pinned directory. Preserve raw result; identity change or unexpected read/parse error remains failure. ENOENT/ESRCH after authenticated exit proof records reaped/missing. Do not follow numeric PID or reap with waitid/waitpid.
recommended_contract.semantic_limit: This proves exit observed after an IO denial within the frozen wait policy. It does not prove exit state or permission cause at the error instant.
recommended_contract.fd_cleanup: Close pidfd and procfd in finally, including partial open/binding failure. Keep descriptor use sequential and bounded.
recommended_contract.accounting: Count proof attempts, terminal missing-IO cases, wait allowance/actual duration and budget exhaustion. Include added pidfd/FD reads and wait time in telemetry cost.

mandatory_failure_states: changed pinned identity before or after error
io EPERM/EIO or other nontransient errors
unavailable/invalid recheck other than explicitly permitted ENOENT/ESRCH
per-task deadline or shared wait budget exhaustion
evidence_on_every_denial: initial raw stat and parsed identity
immediate raw recheck or its error
counterexamples: Live task changes credentials/dumpability and remains alive: EACCES cannot become harmless without terminal proof.
Live task changes permissions and then exits within 50 ms: terminal proof is valid, but the cause of denial remains unknown; preserve it as missing terminal IO.
Old task is reaped, PID is reused before opening procdir: expected start mismatch must stop; a ready old pidfd is not proof about the new proc task.
Leader is terminal but sibling threads remain: process pidfd can remain unreadable; do not substitute leader state as whole-group completion.
Immediate pinned stat disappears after IO denial: ENOENT alone is insufficient; only previously bound pidfd completion may justify the new terminal classification.
EINTR, repeated denied processes, or millisecond rounding must not reset/inflate fixed deadlines; retain actual wait duration and scheduling overshoot.
validation: No implementation or tests executed by this review. Root owns bounded CPU mock/kernel contracts and later real lifecycle validation.
